samples.summary: PUT /content validation is one level stricter than the writer, the reader and the DOCX importer, so it 400s content the rest of the system produces and serves
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` now throws when *any block* sits at `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`. But the accepted model everywhere else is "no *table block* at depth >= cap": `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:231-241) only refuses a table at depth >= cap, `treeNodeToBlock` materializes tables at depths 0…cap-1 with their cell blocks at depth cap, and `DocxImporter.convertTable` deliberately imports a chain of exactly `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` tables (packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:431-437; pinned by packages/docs/test/import/docx-importer.test.ts asserting `importedDepth === MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`). The deepest table there is at depth cap-1 and its cell paragraph is at depth cap → rejected by this validator. Reachable consumers: the CLI's import/replace flow, which PUTs exactly that model (packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:171-181), and a plain GET→edit→PUT round-trip of any document using the full readable nesting depth (also reachable from the editor, whose `insertTable` guard at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4232 permits creating a table at depth cap-1). docs/design/rest-api.md documents GET→PUT identity for well-formed bodies.

samples.summary: The new peer-index clamp lives only in `normalizeCellRange`; several consumers loop over `selection.range.tableCellRange` raw
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1788-1793 computes `minR/maxR/minC/maxC` straight from `range.tableCellRange` and loops `for (r = minR; r <= maxR; …)` with no table-derived clamp; same shape at editor.ts:1295-1300, 3841-3848 and 4406-4410, and text-editor.ts:2910-2911 / 3723-3724. The clamp added in this change only applies to ranges that pass through `normalizeCellRange` (selection.ts:203-232). A `tableCellRange` can reach the *local* selection un-normalized via `restoreSelectionFromPresence` (editor.ts:2486-2497, which copies `restoredSel.tableCellRange` verbatim, reading `YorkieDocStore.getPresenceSelection()` — own presence, yorkie-doc-store.ts:3689). If that presence value is ever attacker- or corruption-influenced, an `end.rowIndex` of 1e9 spins these loops; if it is strictly self-written, this is merely an unclamped path left out of step. Fix belongs on these consumers (or by clamping in `setRange`).
searchedFor: grep tableCellRange across packages/docs/src and packages/frontend/src

samples.summary: The new "never overwrite rows this reader never read" refusal covers the replacing writers but not the deleting ones
samples.evidence: `updateBlock`, `updateTableCell`, `setHeader`, `setFooter`, `insertTableRow`, `insertTableColumn` and `writeFullDocument` now consult `replacesTruncatedRows`/`hasTableAtNestingCap`. `deleteBlock`'s tree edit (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2593 `tree.editByPath(blockPath, endPath)`, and the body variant at 2614) and the row/column deleters take no such check, so deleting the block that holds a peer's truncated table removes rows the local reader never materialized — the same replicated deletion the guard exists to prevent, reached through a different door (e.g. `EditorAPI.deleteTable` → `Doc.deleteBlock`, packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4297). Arguably intentional for an explicit delete, but nothing in the code says so.

samples.summary: `Doc.insertRow`/`insertColumn` now silently return; the EditorAPI commands still snapshot, invalidate and render as if the edit happened
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4314-4323 (`insertTableRow`) and 4341-4350 (`insertTableColumn`) call `docStore.snapshot()` before `doc.insertRow(...)`/`doc.insertColumn(...)` and unconditionally `invalidateLayout(); render();` afterwards. With the new early return at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1075 and 1131 these commands become no-ops that still push an undo snapshot and repaint, giving the user an undo entry for nothing and no feedback that the command was declined. (`text-editor.ts:6086`'s Tab path was updated to handle the missing row; these two were not.)

finding.summary: The new peer-index clamp lives only in `normalizeCellRange`; several consumers loop over `selection.range.tableCellRange` raw
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1788-1793 computes `minR/maxR/minC/maxC` straight from `range.tableCellRange` and loops `for (r = minR; r <= maxR; …)` with no table-derived clamp; same shape at editor.ts:1295-1300, 3841-3848 and 4406-4410, and text-editor.ts:2910-2911 / 3723-3724. The clamp added in this change only applies to ranges that pass through `normalizeCellRange` (selection.ts:203-232). A `tableCellRange` can reach the *local* selection un-normalized via `restoreSelectionFromPresence` (editor.ts:2486-2497, which copies `restoredSel.tableCellRange` verbatim, reading `YorkieDocStore.getPresenceSelection()` — own presence, yorkie-doc-store.ts:3689). If that presence value is ever attacker- or corruption-influenced, an `end.rowIndex` of 1e9 spins these loops; if it is strictly self-written, this is merely an unclamped path left out of step. searchedFor: grep tableCellRange across packages/docs/src and packages/frontend/src

verdict.reason: The raw loops do exist as quoted (editor.ts:1788-1793, 1295-1300, 3841-3848, 4406-4422; text-editor.ts:2914-2918, 3723-3727), but the hazard that makes them blocking — an un-normalized, peer/attacker-influenced tableCellRange reaching the LOCAL selection — is not reachable. Peer presence selections are read in exactly one place, docs-view.tsx:248-257, and flow only into PeerCursor.selection, which is consumed through computeSelectionRects -> normalizeRange -> normalizeCellRange (selection.ts:726, 275-294), i.e. the clamped path. The entry point the finding names, restoreSelectionFromPresence (editor.ts:2465-2500), reads getPresenceSelection, which is own presence only: doc.getMyPresence() and getPresenceForTest(own actorID) (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3689-3704); own activeSelection is written from locally resolved anchors (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1588-1601, 1569-1575, 3742-3773). The only other external setter, restoreLocalCursor (editor.ts:4584-4597), is called solely with store.resolveAnchoredLocalCursor() output (docs-view.tsx:434-437). Every local construction of a tableCellRange derives indices from the document/layout (text-editor.ts:2144-2163, 2432-2464, 3373-3383); _setSelectionForTest (editor.ts:4683) is test-only. Hence no 1e9 index can reach these loops; what remains is a locally produced, bounded rectangle whose loops are additionally guarded by rows[r]?.cells[c] — an out-of-step consumer at most (minor), not a reachable bypass of the new guard.

finding.summary: New silent decline in YorkieDocStore.insertTableColumn/insertTableRow leaves Doc.insertColumn/insertRow half-applied — table attrs written without the matching cells/rows
finding.evidence: `YorkieDocStore.insertTableColumn` and `insertTableRow` now `return` without writing when the table sits past the readable nesting cap (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts, `isPastReadableNesting` gates). Their only caller does not know that: `Doc.insertColumn` calls `this.store.insertTableColumn(...)` and then unconditionally `this.store.updateTableAttrs(blockId, { cols: td.columnWidths })` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1061-1062), so the table's `cols` attribute gains a column no cell node exists for — and `treeNodeToBlock`/`computeTableLayout` allocate a cell per (row, column), so the CRDT now permanently describes a wider table than it holds. `Doc.insertRow` has the same shape with `rowHeights` (document.ts:1008-1012). `Doc.mergeCells` (document.ts:1155,1184) loops `store.updateTableCell` per cell, so a per-cell decline leaves a merge half-written. The fix belongs either in the store (decline the attr write too / throw) or in these Doc mutators.

verdict.reason: The claimed half-apply is not present: both Doc mutators decline at the cap before any write. `Doc.insertRow` opens with `if (this.tableNestingDepth(blockId) >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH) return;` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1075), ahead of the `updateTableAttrs` at :1086 and `insertTableRow` at :1088; `Doc.insertColumn` has the identical guard at :1131, ahead of `insertTableColumn` at :1144 and `updateTableAttrs` at :1145. The guard is the same predicate the store declines on: yorkie-doc-store.ts:2956-2957 declines when `rowDepth > MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` and `resolveTableRowDepth` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2936) sets `rowDepth = blockDepth + 1`, i.e. block depth >= 32, while `Doc.tableNestingDepth` (document.ts:200-217) returns the enclosing-table count clamped to the cap. Grep across packages shows the store methods have no other callers than document.ts:1088 and :1144, so there is no bypassing entry point; editor paths (view/editor.ts:4320,4347; view/text-editor.ts:6086) route through the guarded Doc methods. Tests pin the contract (test/model/table-nesting.test.ts:215-224, 226-237). The reviewer's cited lines (1061-1062, 1008-1012) fall in `ensureBlockAfter`, not the table mutators. The ancillary mergeCells remark rests on a different, narrower guard in `updateTableCell` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3112-3121) that only fires when the replaced cell itself holds a cap-depth table with truncated rows — not the decline this finding names, and not its stated fix site.
